body:
Gauss's law states the electric flux through a closed surface is

Choices:
A. Q_enclosed/ε₀
B. ε₀Q_enclosed
C. Q_total outside/ε₀
D. always zero

Energy stored in a capacitor is

Choices:
A. CV²
B. CV²/2
C. C/V²
D. 2C/V

In electrostatic equilibrium, within the conducting material of a conductor, E is

Choices:
A. maximum
B. zero
C. nonzero but uniform throughout
D. time varying

Two point charges remain fixed while their separation triples. The force magnitude becomes

Choices:
A. three times
B. one-third
C. one-ninth
D. one-twenty-seventh

The electric field due to an isolated negative point charge points

Choices:
A. radially outward
B. radially inward
C. tangent to circles
D. its direction depends on the sign of the test charge

For a line charge λ(s), the differential charge element is

Choices:
A. λ ds
B. λ dA
C. λ dV
D. (dλ/ds)ds

Uniform E crosses flat area A whose normal makes angle θ with E. Electric flux is

Choices:
A. EA sinθ
B. EA cosθ
C. EA/ cosθ
D. EA

Charges outside a closed Gaussian surface contribute to

Choices:
A. net enclosed charge
B. local field but zero net flux contribution
C. neither field nor flux anywhere
D. nonzero net flux but no enclosed charge

Two positive point charges are brought closer together. Their electric potential energy

Choices:
A. decreases
B. increases
C. stays zero
D. becomes negative

A positive charge is released from rest and acted on only by a static electric field. It tends toward

Choices:
A. higher potential and higher U
B. lower potential and lower U
C. higher potential and lower U
D. unchanged kinetic energy always

In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field just outside a conductor is

Choices:
A. tangent to the surface
B. normal to the surface
C. zero for every charged conductor
D. parallel to surface current
